subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Grammar Recall: the past perfect tense
outcomes: Understand when we use the past perfect (had + past participle)
Choose between the past perfect and other past forms
Talk about regrets with 'wish' and 'if only'

tf.s: The past perfect is formed with had + past participle.
In 'When I arrived, the lesson had started', the lesson started first.
tf.why: The past perfect shows the earlier action.

tf.s: The past perfect shows the later of two past actions.
tf.why: It shows the earlier of two past actions.

tf.s: We can use 'I wish' + past perfect to talk about regrets.
tf.why: For example, 'I wish I'd started it sooner.'

tf.s: 'If only I had gone to bed earlier' is a regret about the future.
tf.why: It is a regret about the past.

tf.s: The past perfect is correct for every past event.
tf.why: We use it only for the earlier of two past events.

tf.s: 'I'd' can be a short form of 'I had'.
tf.why: 'I'd never lived' means 'I had never lived'.

tf.s: In the listening, B had not expected such a long way between the buildings.
'Had went' is the correct past perfect of 'go'.
In the listening, Sara had expected a huge number of students.

boxes.q: By the time we arrived, the match ___ (finish).
boxes.why: The match ended before we arrived.

boxes.q: I wish I ___ harder for the test.
boxes.why: Wish + past perfect shows a past regret.
If only + past perfect for a past regret.

boxes.q: 'The film had begun when we got to the cinema.' What happened first?
Which words are often followed by the past perfect for regret?
boxes.why: 'I wish I had…' and 'If only I had…'.

boxes.q: What is the past participle of 'eat'?

boxes.why: Hadn't + past participle is the negative past perfect.

boxes.q: What is the short form of 'He had'?
I ___ (live) in Muscat for ten years before we moved.

hunt.q: I'd never lived = I ___ never lived

mcq.q: What does the past perfect show?
o: An action before another past action
mcq.why: It shows which past event came first.

mcq.q: Which sentence has a past perfect verb?
o: I wish I'd started it sooner.

mcq.q: In the listening, what had B not expected about the campus?
o: Such a long way between the buildings
mcq.why: The distance between buildings surprised B.

mcq.q: In the listening, what had Sara expected?
mcq.why: She expected many students and teachers of many nationalities.

mcq.q: Complete: 'When I got home, my brother ___ all the cake.'
mcq.why: He ate the cake before I got home.

mcq.q: Ali stayed up late and is tired today. What does he say?
o: If only I had gone to bed earlier.
If only I go to bed earlier.
If only I am going to bed.
If only I will go to bed earlier.
mcq.why: If only + past perfect for a past regret.

mcq.q: Complete: 'She ___ the sea before she visited Sur.'
mcq.why: Not seeing the sea came before the visit.

mcq.q: Why is the past perfect not always correct for past events?
o: It is used only for the earlier of two past events
It is only for the future
It is never used in writing
mcq.why: For a single past event, the past simple is enough.

mcq.q: 'I'd never lived away from home before I started university.' Which came first?
mcq.why: The past perfect part is the earlier situation.

mcq.q: Why is 'had never seen' correct in 'Before that trip, I had never seen snow'?
o: It happened before another past event
mcq.why: The trip is the later past event.
